plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with latent-factor confounder control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample Salmon raw count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12-row metadata.csv carrying only `condition` (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, human kidney). The profile flags the critical problem: PCA splits the samples into two clusters of six that do NOT track condition, and no batch column was recorded. So the dominant axis of variation in this dataset is an unmeasured factor, and any naive treated-vs-control test is at risk in both directions — inflated false positives if the hidden factor is partially imbalanced across condition, and lost power if it is orthogonal to condition and left in the residual variance.

The plan therefore does three things in order. T1S1 characterizes the hidden structure explicitly and non-negotiably first: recompute the PCA on VST counts, hard-code the two 6-sample clusters as a derived variable `latent_group`, and cross-tabulate it against `condition`. This cross-tab decides everything downstream. If latent_group is exactly orthogonal to condition (3 treated + 3 control per cluster), it is a nuisance factor that can be adjusted for as a blocking term with full retention of the condition contrast. If it is partially confounded (e.g. 5/1), adjustment is possible but the contrast loses power and must be reported with that caveat. If it is perfectly confounded (6/0 — identical to condition), the design is unidentifiable and no method can separate treatment from the hidden factor; the step must say so plainly rather than produce a gene list.

T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 differential expression under the design that T1S1's cross-tab licenses, plus the naive ~condition model as an explicit comparator, so the reader sees how much of the apparent signal is attributable to the latent factor. T1S3 runs an independent, assumption-different confounder estimate — svaseq surrogate variables estimated from the counts without being told the cluster labels — and checks whether the recovered SVs reproduce the observed two-cluster split and whether the SV-adjusted gene list agrees with the cluster-adjusted one. Two routes converging is the only evidence available here that the adjustment is capturing real technical structure rather than carving up biology, since no recorded batch exists to validate against.

T2S1 takes the consensus DE result to hallmark and GO Biological Process enrichment against the staged human MSigDB collections, and is deliberately made to report the naive-model enrichment alongside it so pathway-level conclusions inherit the same confounding caveat as the gene-level ones. Only 12,000 genes are present (a pre-filtered matrix, not a full transcriptome), so the enrichment universe must be restricted to genes actually in the matrix.

Throughout, the honest framing is that the latent factor's identity is unknown. It could be processing batch, sex, RNA quality, tissue sampling region, or genuine subject heterogeneity. Adjusting for it removes its variance whatever it is, but if it is biological rather than technical, the adjusted contrast answers a narrower question than the user posed. The plan requires that this be stated, not buried.

acceptance_criteria: Enrichment is run against human hallmark and human GO Biological Process gene sets resolved from the environment reference store, with the collection and version reported
The gene universe is restricted to the gene symbols present in counts.csv and the universe size is reported
Both over-representation (up and down separately) and rank-based GSEA results are reported with FDR, set size, and leading-edge genes
Hallmark GSEA on the naive Model B ranking is reported alongside the adjusted result, with pathways unique to the naive analysis flagged
If the adjusted DE list is too small for meaningful over-representation (fewer than ~15 significant genes), the step says so and relies on the rank-based GSEA instead of forcing an ORA result
constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens kidney; a mouse or rat collection here would produce confident nonsense
Do not use a whole-genome background; the universe is the pre-filtered 12,000-gene matrix
Report FDR-adjusted values, never raw enrichment p-values, as the headline
Do not claim a treatment mechanism from enrichment alone — enrichment names a program that shifted, not a cause
If either gene set collection is absent at run time, report which one was used and note the reduced coverage rather than substituting a different organism's sets
caveats: Gene symbols in the counts matrix may include deprecated or non-HGNC aliases; report the fraction of the 12,000 symbols that map into the GMT collections
GO BP sets are nested and produce blocks of correlated hits — collapse redundant parent/child terms before reporting a count of enriched processes
With a small adjusted DE list, hallmark GSEA is the more stable readout than ORA and should be given more weight
